title: Start networking from Day 1
description: Don't wait for organized events. Walk up to people in the cafeteria, join Slack channels, and introduce yourself. The connections you make here last a lifetime.

title: Ask 'stupid' questions early
description: There are no stupid questions in the first two weeks. After that, people expect you to know things. Front-load your curiosity.

title: Document everything you learn
description: Keep a daily learning journal. It helps with your mid-review, Demo Day presentation, and future job interviews. You'll forget more than you think.

title: Ship early, iterate fast
description: Don't spend 6 weeks building the perfect thing. Ship a rough version in week 2, get feedback, and iterate. Your mentor wants to see progress, not perfection.

title: Attend every leader session
description: These sessions are gold. Where else do you get to ask a CTO career questions in a room of 24 people? Take notes and follow up.

title: Learn the codebase before coding
description: Spend your first week reading code, not writing it. Understand the architecture, patterns, and conventions. Your PRs will be much better for it.

title: Build relationships with your mentor
description: Your mentor is your biggest advocate. Schedule regular 1:1s, ask for feedback actively, and share your career aspirations. They want to help you succeed.

title: Contribute beyond your project
description: Fix a bug in another team's repo. Write internal blog posts. Organize a tech talk. The interns who stand out are the ones who add value beyond their assigned work.

title: Don't depend on Bengaluru traffic
description: Leave at least 45 minutes early. Bangalore traffic is unpredictable, especially during monsoon. Being late to your first standup sets the wrong tone.

title: Don't skip the social events
description: It's tempting to code through the hackathon social hour or skip the team outing. Don't. The bonds you form outside work are what make the experience special.

title: Don't be afraid to push back
description: If a task feels impossible in the given time, say so. Mentors respect honest communication way more than missed deadlines. Scope negotiation is a skill.

title: Don't compare your progress to others
description: Everyone has different projects, teams, and backgrounds. Focus on your own growth trajectory. The only person you should compete with is yesterday's you.

title: Don't work in isolation
description: Remote days are fine sometimes, but being in the office matters. Watercooler conversations lead to breakthrough ideas. Plus, the cafeteria food is amazing.

title: Don't leave documentation to the last week
description: Document as you go. Your future self (and the next intern inheriting your project) will thank you. Week 12 is too chaotic for writing docs.

title: Don't be intimidated by senior engineers
description: They were interns once too. Most senior engineers love helping interns — it reminds them of their own journey. Ask them for code reviews, they'll say yes.

title: Don't forget to have fun
description: 12 weeks goes by in a flash. Take photos, make memories, try the dessert at the cafeteria, explore the city on weekends. Work hard, but enjoy the ride.

title: Master the art of the standup
description: Keep it under 2 minutes: what you did, what you're doing, what's blocking you. Practice beforehand if you're nervous. Nobody judges you for being concise.

title: Set up your dev environment on Day 1
description: VPN, repo access, build tools, IDE plugins — get it all working before you need it. There's always something that takes 3 hours to configure.

title: Keep a 'wins' file
description: Every time something goes well — a merged PR, positive feedback, a solved bug — write it down. This file is invaluable for your mid-review, Demo Day, and resume.

title: Learn the org structure early
description: Understanding who does what and how teams connect will help you navigate the organization. It also helps you find the right person to unblock you.

title: Prepare for Demo Day from Week 1
description: Start recording screenshots, metrics, and learnings from the beginning. Building a great Demo Day presentation is way easier when you have 12 weeks of artifacts.

title: Find your 'intern buddy'
description: Partner up with another intern for mutual support. Review each other's code, practice presentations together, and debrief after tough days.

title: Use Adobe's internal tools to your advantage
description: Adobe has incredible internal tools for design, analytics, and development. Explore them early — they'll make your project better and give you skills for your resume.

title: Write your PR descriptions like blog posts
description: Explain the 'why' not just the 'what'. Include screenshots, before/after comparisons, and testing notes. Great PR descriptions get faster reviews and more feedback.

title: Present at the internal tech talks
description: Volunteer to present something — even a 5-minute lightning talk. It builds your visibility, communication skills, and confidence. Start small, think big.

title: Learn from code reviews, not just your own
description: Subscribe to PRs from senior engineers on your team. Reading their code reviews teaches you more about software craft than any tutorial.

title: Build your project with the next intern in mind
description: Someone will inherit your code. Write READMEs, add comments for non-obvious decisions, and create onboarding docs. Your code's legacy outlasts your internship.

title: The cafeteria filter coffee is underrated
description: Skip the fancy machine. The South Indian filter coffee from the cafeteria is the best-kept secret at Adobe Bengaluru. Trust us on this one.
